$schema_note: Visa/vaccine/insurance entry-requirement guidance, requested by the user 2026-09-02 ('tabela de country regulation'). IMPORTANT, read before trusting or extending this file: this is compiled from general knowledge, not verified against each country's official government/embassy source, and is NOT exhaustive - it covers the 18 curated Destination countries plus roughly 25 other major destinations, not all ~195 UN member states. Some entries (flagged inline via 'confidence': 'low' where present) cover genuinely volatile situations (e.g. Brazil's reciprocal visa policy toward US/Canada/Australia has changed direction multiple times in recent years; Russia's visa relationships with Western countries are actively shifting; China has been expanding unilateral visa-free entry for various countries) where the general pattern described may already be stale. travel.services.ENTRY_REQUIREMENT_DISCLAIMER must accompany this data wherever it is shown - see travel/models.py's CountryEntryRequirement docstring for why. visa_required_nationalities lists are deliberately representative (major/commonly-relevant nationalities), not exhaustive enumerations of all countries - see each entry's visa_notes for the general exemption structure instead, which is the more reliable and more compact way to describe most countries' policies. Translated from the original Portuguese to English (canonical source language, matching curated_destinations.json) on 2026-09-08 - see DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md for why. The 'country' field must stay in sync with curated_destinations.json's country spellings - note this file uses 'USA' for the United States (not 'United States'), matching the original dataset's 'EUA' abbreviation once translated. 'videos' (added 2026-09-07, direct user request) is a separate, unrelated caveat of its own: real YouTube URLs found via live web search (never fabricated - each one was verified to exist in an actual search result before being added here), as [url, language_code] pairs - not vetted against an official tourism board catalog, and video availability/content can change or be taken down after the fact, so treat this the same as any other unverified-third-party-source field in this file.

countries.visa_notes: As a Schengen country, it follows the bloc's common policy: EU/EEA citizens enter freely; dozens of nationalities (USA, Canada, United Kingdom, Australia, Japan, South Korea, and most of Latin America, including Brazil and Argentina) can enter visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. From 2025, visa-exempt travelers also need ETIAS authorization before boarding. Most of Africa and part of Asia need a Schengen visa.
countries.insurance_notes: Those who need a Schengen visa must show travel insurance with minimum coverage of €30,000 for medical emergencies.
other_requirements: Passport valid for at least 3 months after the planned departure date

countries.visa_notes: The Visa Waiver Program (VWP) covers about 40 countries - most of the EU, United Kingdom, Japan, South Korea, Australia, among others - who can enter for up to 90 days with ESTA authorization instead of a visa. The vast majority of other countries, including nearly all of Latin America (Brazil, Argentina, and neighbors), need a traditional tourist visa (B1/B2), with a consulate interview.
